addresses: Promoting the whole invite card put zero of eleven people on the admin's first screen; Marcus Webb, the June leaver, starts 2.2 viewports down (visual-phone, major)
The invite-first decision was right; spending 279px of empty form plus 456px of already-sent invitations to reach a single email field is what costs
changes.change: Below `lg` the Invited card is collapsed to its header: a 68px row reading `Invited [4]` with a `＋ Invite someone` affordance on the right, and the whole card body — form first, then the four invitation rows — opens on one tap. At `lg` and up the card is exactly as it was: header, form, four rows, always open, no affordance. The first roster row moved from y=1114 to y=357, Marcus Webb from y=1868 to y=1110 (2.2 viewports → 1.3), and the phone page fell from 2693px to 1935px. Three names are now on the first screen. The two card subtitles are `hidden lg:block` — at 326px of content they are boilerplate competing with the header row's action.
changes.rationale: Collapsing only the form leaves the roster card 20px below the fold — I built that first and measured it: header 68 + four 113px rows still consumes the viewport, so zero names. The four invitations are what is left, and capping them at two with a 'show all' expander would have hidden the one suspended invitation, which is the opposite of what this screen is for. Collapsing the card whole is one mechanism instead of two, keeps every invitation reachable, and keeps round 1's promotion honest: what is promoted is now the action (a 44px tap at the top of the page) rather than an inert form. The count badge still says four before you open it.
changes.breakpoint: below `lg` — at `lg` and up nothing changes

addresses: The Active toggle is a click 626px right of the name and nothing on the row binds them; a click one row off revokes the wrong adult (visual-desktop, major)
The only row boundary is a 1.18:1 rule; the `<li>` carries no hover at all
changes.change: Every roster row (both scenes, editable and read-only) gets a full-bleed pointer-only hover wash: `@2xl:pointer-fine:hover:bg-ink-800/40`. The whole 712px strip — name, recency, role, toggle — lights as one object under the cursor. The divider is untouched.
changes.rationale: The wash is the cheapest thing that makes the row a single target, and it costs the touch layouts nothing because it is gated on `pointer: fine` as well as on the container width — a wide touch tablet would otherwise leave a row lit under a finger that has moved on. I did not thicken the divider: two row-separation devices where one will do, and the critic said the divider can stay faint once the band exists.
changes.breakpoint: container `@2xl` (row >= 42rem) and `pointer: fine` — desktop only in practice
changes.implementation: `TeamPage.tsx`, roster `<li>`: append `@2xl:pointer-fine:hover:bg-ink-800/40` to the className. Tailwind emits it from the existing `@container` on the `<ul>` and the app's `pointer-fine` variant; no new token.

addresses: The read-only view inherits the admin's four-column grid and has nothing for the fourth column, so a 680px identity cell strands the facts 500px from the name (design-desktop, major)
541px of void between an address and its recency, another 165px empty to the right of the role badge (visual-desktop, minor)
changes.change: The read-only roster no longer shares the admin's grid. Its row is `@2xl:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_10.5rem_7.5rem]` — three columns, no trailing empty one — and the card is capped at `lg:max-w-3xl` (768px), which is within a few pixels of the width the admin's roster card gets beside the 24rem invite column. Recency now starts at x=703 instead of x=969 and the role sits at x=886; the identity cell is 416px instead of 680px. Same read, same reading distance, on both permission levels.
changes.rationale: Both critics offered 'cap the column' or 'cap the card'; capping the card does both and is the only one that also removes the dead band after the role. Leaving 384px as outer margin is cheaper than leaving it inside the row, and eleven rows already fit — the density this page owed was rows above the fold, not ink per pixel.
changes.breakpoint: `lg` and up for the card cap; container `@2xl` for the column set. Below `lg` neither applies.
changes.implementation: `TeamPage.tsx`: the page grid wrapper becomes `cn('grid gap-4', isAdmin ? 'lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_24rem] lg:items-start lg:gap-6' : 'lg:max-w-3xl')`. The roster `<li>` takes its grid template from `canEdit`: admin `@2xl:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_10.5rem_7.5rem_6.5rem]`, read-only `@2xl:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_10.5rem_7.5rem]`. Drop the `@2xl:col-span-2` from the read-only badge cluster.

addresses: The same Active control sits in two lanes on one scrolling page — x=32–119 on invitations, x=158–243 on members (visual-phone, minor)
Neither control strip shares an edge with the text above it; the padded controls' insets leak out as layout (design-phone, minor)
'Suspended' and 'Never signed in' occupy three different positions across the two lists (design-phone, minor)
One token, two structural homes: the danger badge rides the name line in the roster and trails the meta sentence in an invitation (design-desktop, minor)
The read-only row is a four-item stack whose fourth item is the only filled shape, and the constant role is boxed while the variable recency is not (design-phone / design-desktop, minor)
changes.change: One lane rule, applied in both lists and at both permission levels. (a) Badges mark exceptions only. The neutral `Counselor` capsule on the read-only rows is now plain `text-xs text-ink-400`; elevated roles (Admin, Core team) keep the ring, and on the admin page the self row's `Admin` badge became plain `text-sm text-ink-100` so the role column is one vocabulary rather than one brand slab among eleven words. (b) An exception badge leads its line, never trails it. The invitation's `Suspended` now sits at the front of the meta line, before 'Counselor · invited 24 days ago'. (c) The state toggle owns the row's trailing edge: both lists are `justify-between` — role select (or `Withdraw`) at the leading edge, `Active` hard right. (d) The padded controls' optical edges land on the row's text edges — `-ml-4` on `Withdraw`, `-mr-2 @2xl:mr-0` on the `Active` label. (e) On the read-only phone row the role token leaves the identity's lane and sits on the recency line's right edge, so the row is three lines with two columns instead of four stacked items; row height fell 105px → 77px and the core phone page 1782px → 1320px, with Marcus Webb now on the first screen.
changes.rationale: Four findings and one shape: the screen had badges doing two jobs (naming a role, flagging a state) and one control living in two places. Making badges mean 'exception' is what lets (b) and (e) work — once `Counselor` is text, Hannah's warn badge is not stacked above a pill of the same shape, and the exception is the only capsule in its row. I put the invitation's `Suspended` at the head of the meta line rather than beside the address, which is what the desktop critic asked for and round 1 declined: a 31-character address plus a 78px badge fits the 352px column today but truncates on a longer one, and truncating an address on the screen that matches people by address is the wrong economy. Leading the meta line gets the same 'one vertical position per row' the phone critic asked for without that risk. Putting `Withdraw` at the leading edge rather than the trailing one is a bonus on a phone: the reversible control is where the thumb lands and the destructive one is not.
changes.breakpoint: both. (c) and (d) are the phone/stacked layout; at `@2xl` the roster's columns already fix the lane and `@2xl:mr-0` puts the toggle back on its column start. (e) is below `@2xl` only — at width the grid already reads that way.

Control strips: roster cluster `flex shrink-0 flex-wrap items-center justify-between gap-4 @2xl:contents`; invitation cluster keeps `flex items-center justify-between gap-4` but renders `Withdraw` first with `className="-ml-4 …"`; the `AccessToggle` label gains `-mr-2 … @2xl:mr-0`. Read-only phone row: wrap the recency `

` and the role cluster in `

addresses: The address is 12px at 3.75:1 — the least legible text on a screen about who may reach a roster of minors (visual-phone, minor)
Let the recency value step up one notch so it clearly outranks the email it sits beside (design-desktop, minor)
changes.change: The member row's email went `text-ink-500` → `text-ink-400` (3.75:1 → ~7:1, clears AA at 12px) and the recency went `text-ink-400` → `text-ink-300` (~11.6:1). The ranking is preserved and sharpened: name > recency > address. The self row's 'Another admin has to change this.' note took the same step to `text-ink-400`.
changes.rationale: Two findings pull opposite ways — one wants the address up, the other wants recency to stay clearly above it — and a single step for each satisfies both rather than flattening them into one value. I left the invitation meta line and the card subtitles at ink-500: those are 14px reference prose, not the 12px cited failure, and moving them would be a ramp change for the whole app made inside a screen round.

addresses: The largest, most saturated mass on the screen is inert and its label sits at 2.1:1 against its own fill (visual-phone and design-phone, minor — raised independently by both)
changes.change: The disabled primary submit sheds presence instead of legibility: `disabled:bg-ink-800 disabled:text-ink-400 disabled:opacity-100`. The empty-form Invite button is now a quiet ink slab with a 6:1 label; it regains the brand fill when the form is valid.
changes.rationale: Two critics, one class list, and the current state is an outright contrast failure rather than a taste question. I scoped it to the disabled state of the primary variant, not to the resting appearance of anything — every disabled primary in Tally improves identically and nothing that is usable changes. That is the difference from round 1's declined `CONTROL` background change, which would have restyled every field in the app at rest.

Ghost and other variants keep the opacity treatment — they have no fill to lose.

The page subtitle is one unbroken 766px line aligned to nothing, while the disclosure beneath it is capped narrower (design-desktop, minor)

The deck takes the disclosure's measure — `max-w-2xl` — so the header block is one column of prose instead of two measures, and the deck no longer hangs into the gutter between the cards.
changes.rationale: Both are one class each and both were asked for. Value and weight are enough to say 'this opens' without giving the summary a box back — the box is what round 1 correctly removed.

declined.finding: The recency column re-states 'Last seen ' on every row; the table has earned a header row with bare values in it (visual-desktop, minor).
declined.why: Real, and the argument from Hannah's flush warn badge is a good one. But it is a new structural element on two scenes and two permission levels — a header row that must carry different labels for the admin grid (Role, Access) and the read-only one, plus a responsive prefix (`Last seen ` visible below `@2xl`, hidden above it, because a bare '11 days ago' on a phone has no column heading to lean on). This round already re-cut the read-only grid; adding a header row on top of that in the same pass means the next critic judges two changes at once and cannot tell which one is wrong. It is the first thing to do next round if the grid holds.

declined.finding: Sticky card headers on the phone would stop the two lists blurring together at scroll depth (visual-phone, minor).
declined.why: The finding was that a thumb cannot tell which of two Active-checkbox lists it is in. That condition no longer holds: below `lg` the invitation list is inside a collapsed card, so a scrolling admin is in exactly one list, and the two lists now use one control lane anyway. A sticky header would be new scroll machinery answering a problem the layout change removed.

declined.finding: Ten solid brand ticks are the most saturated stripe on the page and encode the state that needs no attention; bring the majority state down (design-desktop, minor).
declined.why: Declined in round 1 and the reason has not changed. Chrome draws `accent-color` checkboxes itself, so the checked mark cannot be stepped down the ramp without `appearance-none` and a hand-drawn box — a new drawing in a shared control for one screen's benefit — and a quieter tick risks converging with the unchecked box, which is the one distinction on this page that must never blur. What I did instead is lower the noise around it: the role capsules are gone from the read-only column, the self row's brand badge is gone from the admin column, and brand is now doing two jobs in the frame rather than four.

declined.finding: Two people on this roster are admins and they are drawn in two visual languages — Dana's filled brand badge versus Eli's quiet select text (visual-desktop, minor).
declined.why: Half done. Dana's badge is now plain `text-ink-100` text, so the role column is one vocabulary and the loudest object in it is no longer the one role that cannot be changed. The other half — 'spot two marks rather than read eleven words' — would mean rendering the select as a badge with the control as its hover skin, which is a new control drawing, and it fights the change round 1 made to quiet the selects at rest. Reading eleven role words in a 120px column is a real cost but a small one; a bespoke select-that-looks-like-a-pill is not a small change.

declined.finding: Let the access cell's word follow its state — Active / Suspended — so the confirmation of a revoke happens where the click happened (visual-desktop, major, second half).
declined.why: A checkbox whose label changes with its own value stops being a labelled property and starts reading as an imperative: an unchecked box next to the word 'Suspended' invites the reading 'click to suspend', which is the inverse of the truth. 'Active' is the name of the thing the box controls. The binding problem the finding is really about — a click landing on the wrong human — is answered by the hover band, which lights the name and the toggle as one object while the pointer travels.

declined.finding: Attach the Suspended badge to the identity line in the invitation as well as in the roster (design-desktop, minor).
declined.why: Partially declined; see the lane-rule change. The badge now leads the meta line rather than trailing it, which gives the reader one place to look at the start of the block. Putting it on the address line fits this seed (31 characters plus a 78px badge inside a 352px column) but truncates a longer address, and the address is the string Tally matches sign-in against. The phone critic asked for exactly this compromise; the desktop critic asked for the stricter version. I took the one that cannot destroy data on a row that is longer than the seed.

declined.finding: The banner promises that some admins are pinned by the deployment and no row ever says which (visual-desktop round 1, major).
declined.why: Still not landable. `TALLY_ADMIN_EMAILS` lives in Functions config and nothing in `users/{id}` or `useAuth` tells the browser that a given admin is pinned, so any UI here would be a picture of a state the client cannot compute. The fix is a data change first — have the auth trigger that re-asserts the claim write `pinned: true` onto the user document, expose it on `UserProfile`, then treat `member.pinned` exactly as `isSelf` is treated in `TeamPage.tsx`. Carried forward unchanged from round 1.
